draft.title: Photosynthesis and respiration in the carbon cycle
card: Photosynthesis
Plants, algae and some bacteria use light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen. This takes carbon dioxide out of the air or water and puts the carbon into living things.
Respiration
Cells break down glucose to release energy, and carbon dioxide is released. Plants, animals and fungi all respire, so all of them return carbon dioxide to the air or water.
Animals get carbon by eating plants or other animals. The carbon in their bodies came from photosynthesis.
Together, the two processes move carbon between the atmosphere and living things. When photosynthesis and respiration are about equal, the amount of carbon dioxide in the air stays steady.
draft.remember: Photosynthesis moves carbon from the air into living things. Respiration moves it back.

a.q: Which process in a eucalyptus tree takes carbon dioxide from the air and builds it into glucose?
opts: Photosynthesis
Respiration
Digestion
Decomposition
a.why: Photosynthesis uses light energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into glucose. Respiration is the tempting answer, but it does the reverse: it breaks glucose down and releases carbon dioxide.

b.q: Priya says that only animals release carbon dioxide, because plants only take it in. Which reply is correct?
opts: Plants also respire, so they release carbon dioxide too
Plants only release oxygen, so they never give out carbon
Plants respire only at night, so they release it then only
Plants release carbon dioxide only when they are dying
b.why: Plant cells break down glucose in respiration, so plants release carbon dioxide as well as taking it in. The tempting option about night is wrong, because the card says respiration happens in all of these living things and is not limited to darkness.
b.clue: Which living things respire, according to the card?

b.best: Plants also respire, so they release carbon dioxide too

problems.detail: Every wrong option uses 'only' or 'never' and the right option is the only one without an absolute word, so a test-wise student could pick it without knowing the idea.
The why says the card states respiration 'is not limited to darkness', but the card says nothing about day or night. It only says plants, animals and fungi all respire.
